facts.fact: The Mauritius Judiciary's notices say attorneys at the Commercial Division must file written submissions online through the e-filing system and apply online for subpoenas, new features introduced from 11 January 2021.

L'Express reported in July 2023 that the Judiciary's existing Case Management System was maintained by State Informatics to July 2021 and that some courts, notably the Family Division, have been computerised since 2021.
L'Express reported in July 2023 that the e-judiciary project, with e-filing and case management, was 40% implemented that year and phase 2 was not complete.

Chief Justice Bernard Sik Yuen launched the first phase of the E-Judiciary service at the Supreme Court on 4 April 2013, letting lawyers submit documents and enter commercial cases online, with family and criminal cases to follow.

facts.fact: News Moris, citing l'Express, says Mauritius's e-judiciary project, announced over a decade earlier, is still in its pilot phase in June 2024.
The article says e-filing of documents currently exists only at the commercial court, though lawyers still have to attend court physically after uploading.

note: A Children's Court case management system and an e-judiciary service are budget announcements only, with no procurement, pilot or build stated.
